source_documents.title: Self‐Amplifying AIE Probe for HClO‐Activatable Imaging and Antioxidative/Anti‐Inflammatory Therapy of Thoracic Aortic Dissection

reference_evidence_units.quote: The probe initially exhibits quenched fluorescence via photoinduced electron transfer (PET).
reference_evidence_units.subject: DT-PZ
reference_evidence_units.statement: The free probe is dark because of PET.

reference_evidence_units.quote: both probes underwent efficient a-PET, where an electron from the excited fluorophore (10-methylphenothiazine or phenothiazine) was transferred to the receptor unit (pyridinium salt-modified triphenylamine).
reference_evidence_units.subject: DT-PZM, DT-PZ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Frontier orbitals place the electron donor on the phenothiazine and the acceptor on the pyridinium-TPA.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Notably, phenothiazine exhibited a higher-lying HOMO compared to 10-methylphenothiazine, which enhanced the driving force for a-PET [36]. As a result, DT-PZ demonstrated more complete FL quenching and lower background signal, in full agreement with experimental observations.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DT-PZ vs DT-PZM
reference_evidence_units.statement: N-H phenothiazine is the stronger donor: more complete quenching than the N-methyl analogue.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, no significant FL signal was detected for DT-PZ under identical conditions, indicating its negligible background FL.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DT-PZ vs DT-PZM
reference_evidence_units.statement: DT-PZM shows weak emission near 650 nm; DT-PZ shows none.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Upon oxidation of the sulfur atom in 10-methylphenothiazine or phenothiazine to sulfoxide by HClO, the electron-donating ability of the donor was substantially diminished, thereby blocking the PET pathway and turning on strong FL.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DT-PZ, DT-PZM + HClO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Sulfoxide formation removes the donor and turns emission on.

reference_evidence_units.quote: As the THF fraction increased, the FL of both DTPZM and DT-PZ was significantly enhanced, revealing a typical AIE characteristic.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DT-PZM, DT-PZ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission rises on aggregation (AIE index 18.7 for DT-PZ, 5.2 for DT-PZM).

reference_evidence_units.quote: As depicted, the twisted triphenylamine rotor can facilitate nonradiative decay via intramolecular rotation in the single molecule, resulting in low FL background.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DT-PZM, DT-PZ
reference_evidence_units.statement: The TPA rotor gives rotation-driven nonradiative decay in the isolated molecule.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a lower-energy band around 420 nm, characteristic of a typical intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) process.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DT-PZM, DT-PZ
reference_evidence_units.statement: The low-energy absorption band is a D-A ICT band.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: AIE on aggregation, assigned to the TPA rotor's rotation-driven nonradiative decay in the isolated molecule.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Paper's explanation of the dark free probe: a-PET from the phenothiazine to the pyridinium-TPA receptor (DFT), stronger than in the N-methyl analogue; oxidation of the donor turns emission on.

out_of_pool: PROBE_REACTION: HClO oxidation of the phenothiazine sulfur to the sulfoxide blocks PET (emission of the reaction product) (E05)

contrast_group.paper_difference: The N-H phenothiazine has the higher HOMO, a larger PET driving force and no background emission; the N-methyl probe keeps weak emission near 650 nm.

structure_verification.note: Tetracation; the paper gives the pyridinium salts from iodomethane (iodide counterions), SMILES carries the dye cation only.
basis: SI route: 3,7-dibromo-10-Boc-phenothiazine (HRMS C17H15Br2NO2S) + bis(4-pyridylphenyl)aminophenyl arms, Boc ester 8 (HRMS C73H55N7O2S), N-methylation of the four pyridines and deprotection
